window_mix.note: extended_cases were re-measured ONLY after failing the convergence gate at the modal window; no case that already passed was re-rolled. paired_ab_bound_pct is the largest per-case move seen in a same-case paired A/B between the modal and the extended window (null = not established for this operator, which is NOT the same as zero).

cases.flops_note: IMGWarpOffsets pure indexed copy: the only arithmetic on the chain is the per-channel index bias idx+c, i.e. 192 integer adds (64 offsets x 3 channels).  The gather, the int64 promotion and the Pack are addressing/movement with no FLOPs, so MFU is structurally ~0 here and the shipped 1.4142651e-08% (from a literal flops=1.0) is not comparable with this value.  DO NOT read achieved_bw_gbs as the alternative either: it divides ALGORITHMIC in/out (384 bytes here) by time, which makes it a STRICT LOWER BOUND on traffic and NOT comparable with sibling operators.  The chain materialises far more (a 64x3 int64 index, 3 gather outputs, the packed result), but the chain figure is only a LOOSE UPPER bound: case 44's ~2416 MB over 117.8 ms would be 20.5 TB/s, above this part's ~1.2-1.4 TB/s, so those intermediates are not all HBM round-trips.  Both ends are unusable, and so is any bandwidth or MFU figure for 19 -- the measured truth is a PIPE breakdown, not a rate: see the source NOTE for 19 (the 3x GatherElementsV2 report aiv_scalar_ratio 0.999 with aiv_vec_ratio 0.0005 and aiv_mte2_ratio 0.0008 -- the cost is on the SCALAR pipe, not on the vector ALU and not on the bulk-copy pipes, so 19 is neither flops-bound nor bandwidth-bound.  (The counters say the scalar pipe is OCCUPIED; they do NOT say instructions are being issued at that rate -- 189 cycles/output-element would be far too many for the ~6-10 instructions a gather needs, so stall/wait is plausibly included.  Do not read it as a proven issue-bound rate.)  The only rate that is comparable for this operator is per-element throughput, and it is STRONGLY SIZE-DEPENDENT -- so do NOT quote one case as the operator's rate.  Measured on the four kept captures, one gather kernel runs 5.8 M elem/s at 16 output elements (case 24), 50.7 at 128 (case 0), 420.2 at 1.05 M (case 40) and 439.5 at 16.8 M (case 44): a 76x spread, because the small cases are launch-bound and their per-element rate collapses.  The large-case plateau is ~420-440 M elem/s (2.3 us per 1000 elements), and that plateau is the only figure worth quoting.

Caliber: warmup=25, repeats=10, per-case msprof capture, trailing-10 mean; gap-fenced iteration segmentation (instrumented sync+sleep separator, floor 9 ms); convergence gate = |drift| <= 5% on mean(2nd half of last 10)/mean(1st half), judged separately for e2e and core. MFU DENOMINATOR CHANGED (pre-delivery, 2026-09-13): all ten CV operators are now divided by the vector peak 48 x 0.2304 = 11.0592 TFLOPS (48 measured -- the framework's own Transpose kernels launch at Block Dim = 48; cross-checked against the archived profile's 'AI Core Freq 1800 MHz'), instead of the 353.8944 fp16 Cube peak used by the previously shipped 12-21 perf.json. MFU here is therefore ~32x the shipped file's. This is a caliber unification, NOT a statement that the engines are uniform -- measured per case they are not: 12/15/16/19 are pure AI_VECTOR_CORE, 13 adds MIX_AIV, 14 runs MIX_AIC on 34 of 47 cases and really occupies the Cube (cube_utilization 85-95%), and 17/18/20/21 carry AI_CPU cases that never reach an AI Core. The vector peak is exact only for the pure-AIV operators; for 14 the Cube peak is arguably closer, and for AI_CPU cases neither applies. MFU is a tie-breaker in this pipeline -- quote it with achieved_bw_gbs, never alone. Per-operator engine mix: OPT_HINTS.md. FORMAT NOTICE (added 2026-09-13): this file does NOT carry an accuracy verdict. The previously shipped 12-21 perf.json had `accuracy_passed_cases` (top level) and a per-case `accuracy`; the schema used here records `cases_valid` (a usable msprof capture was obtained) and `cases_converged` (the |drift| <= 5% gate passed) instead -- NEITHER is an accuracy statement, and neither should be read as one. Unlike 20 and 21 there is NO dispatch split: the per-iteration kernel multiset is IDENTICAL for all 50 cases, read out of msprof op_summary rather than inferred -- Cast x4, Add x3, GatherElementsV2 x3, Pack x1 = 11 kernels/iteration, and every one of them is AI_VECTOR_CORE with aicore_time = 0 (this operator never touches the Cube, so any MFU quoted against the 353.8944 TFLOP/s fp16 cube peak is quoted against the wrong engine). CONSEQUENCE FOR core_us COMPARABILITY, stated because the rest of this file cannot be read without it: core_us here is ENGINE-CLEAN. Every core op runs on AI_VECTOR_CORE, so core_us contains no AICPU time and no MIX time -- unlike 17/18/20/21, where core_us silently includes AI_CPU work (21 ~3/4 of it, 20's ac=T cases 91-94%) because measure.py's core filter keys on the op NAME and never on task_type. So 19 is directly comparable with 12/15/16 in engine terms and NOT comparable with 17/18/20/21. But read the corollary too: engine-clean does NOT mean AI-Core-bound -- see the pipe breakdown below, whose conclusion is that neither AI Core compute pipe is the binding resource here. The chain is the repo Model verbatim: offsets.to(int64) [Cast] -> idx+c for c in 0,1,2 [Add] -> 3x torch.gather(images_flat, 1, idx+c) [GatherElementsV2] -> torch.stack [Pack]; the two reshapes are free views. The glue-stripped core ops are therefore Add + GatherElementsV2 + Pack. ROUTE: the shipped _perf.json names 'ops-cv image_warp_offsets (torch.gather 向量化) aclnn 实测', and this adapter is deliberately a pure delegate to npu_benchmark/level3/19_deformable_offsets.py::Model, which IS that torch.gather vectorisation (its own docstring says so) and whose JSONL op name is IMGWarpOffsets. The torch route is forced, not chosen, and the reason is stronger than 'we did not find a driver': ops-ref/ops-cv/image/image_warp_offsets ships an AICPU implementation ONLY -- op_kernel_aicpu/image_warp_offsets_aicpu.{h,cpp}, with NO op_kernel/ directory, no op_host/config/ at all, and not one mention of ascend910b anywhere in the op directory. So there is no AscendC AI Core kernel for this operator to compare against in the first place, and an AICPU implementation would not be an AI-Core-caliber comparator even if it ran (the same caution NOTE_21 records for AffineGrid). The CANN side agrees: an aicpu::ImageWarpOffsetsCpuKernel does exist in opp/built-in/op_impl/host_aicpu/libcpu_kernels.so, but there is NO aclnnImageWarpOffsets symbol in libopapi.so and NO ImageWarpOffsets op type in any of the six aic-ascend910b-ops-info-*.json tables (the nearest name, legacy IMGWarpResize, is the RESIZE variant, not offsets). The other lookalike is a trap that has already been checked and rejected: legacy DeformableOffsets IS registered and compiled for 910b, but its semantics differ (it takes (dy,dx) coordinate offsets plus REQUIRED strides/pads/ksize and interpolates bilinearly, whereas this operator treats the offset as a linear index and copies 3 channels with no interpolation) -- using it would measure a different operator. CAVEAT on the numeric check: wrapper.py --check case 0 reports max_abs_diff 0.000e+00, but for a delegate that is tautological (it compares the Model against itself); it confirms wiring and shapes only. The route evidence is the above, NOT the check. WHERE THE TIME GOES: the 3 GatherElementsV2 out of 11 kernels dominate as soon as the operator is not launch-bound -- 51% of core_us on case 0 (7.58 of 14.82 us) but 97.6-97.8% on cases 40/44 (114.5 of 117.1 ms on case 44). WHY, read off the pipe counters rather than assumed -- the cost lands ENTIRELY ON THE SCALAR PIPE. On case 44 its aiv_scalar_time is 36604.3 of an aiv_time of 36650.9 us (aiv_scalar_ratio 0.9990, agreeing with 0.9988 computed directly), against aiv_vec_time 16.8 us (vec ratio 0.0005) and aiv_mte2_time 18.8 us (mte2 ratio 0.0008); aic_mac_time is 0 and cube_utilization is 0. Case 40 is the same (scalar ratio 0.9969). So the memory pipes AND the vector ALU are both idle to ~0.05% while the scalar pipe reports itself busy throughout. The per-element mechanism is NOT resolved by these counters and is deliberately not asserted here: aiv_scalar_time saturating says the scalar pipe is occupied, not that instructions are being ISSUED at that rate. The arithmetic warns against the naive reading -- 16777216 outputs over 48 blocks is 349525 outputs per core, so 36650 us is 104.9 ns = ~189 cycles per output element at 1.8 GHz, whereas a gather needs on the order of 6-10 instructions per element, which at 1 IPC would be 3-6% of aiv_time, not 100%. Something is being counted that is not pure issue (stall/wait attributed to the scalar pipe, and/or an uneven 48-block split). THE SCALAR SHARE GROWS WITH SIZE -- scalar/aiv is 0.71 on case 0, 0.44-0.46 on Add/Pack, and 0.997-0.999 on the large gathers. What IS safe to say: this is a scalar-LOAD-driven gather (aiv_mte2_ratio 0.0008 = no bulk MTE2 transfer is carrying the data), so its cost falls on the scalar pipe, and 19 is neither flops-bound nor bandwidth-bound. The only comparable RATE for this operator is per-element throughput, and it must NOT be quoted from a single case because it is STRONGLY SIZE-DEPENDENT. Measured on the four kept captures (one gather kernel, last-30-iteration mean): 5.8 M elem/s at 16 output elements (case 24), 50.7 at 128 (case 0), 420.2 at 1.05 M (case 40), 439.5 at 16.8 M (case 44) -- a 76x spread, because the small cases are launch-bound and their per-element rate collapses. The large-case plateau is ~420-440 M elem/s (2.3 us per 1000 elements); quote the plateau with its size range, not a point. COUNTER-SOURCE (added 2026-09-13): the pipe ratios quoted above (aiv_scalar 0.999, aiv_vec 0.0005, aiv_mte2 0.0008) and the per-element rates are DERIVED FROM THE KEPT RAW op_summary CAPTURES under keep_evidence/19_deformable_offsets/case_{0,24,40,44}/ -- they are NOT fields of this JSON file. At the time of writing this file carried no per-pipe-counter or per-element-rate key, so grepping it for those quantities only hits this sentence; if ANY later revision exposes a field for these quantities, prefer that field and treat this note as superseded. Two consequences that must not be glossed: (a) '19 is bandwidth bound' is FALSE, so a memory-pipe roofline does not apply to it; accounting for 48 blocks over 114.5 ms of scalar pipe is what the operator actually costs. (b) the int64 promotion in the Model is a pure ROUND TRIP: the captured Cast signatures on case 44 are INT32->INT64 on (4,16,512,512) once per iteration (the Model's .to(int64)) and INT64->INT32 on (4,4194304) three times per iteration -- i.e. each aclnn gather immediately casts the index back down to int32 before gathering, which is why Cast appears 4x per iteration and why the aclnnGather_GatherElementsV2_GatherElementsV2 row reports Input Data Types FLOAT16;INT32 despite the int64 index. CONSEQUENCE for the 50-case geomean: 40 of the 50 cases are launch-floor bound (core_us 13.7-22 us for an 11-kernel chain, i.e. ~1.3 us per kernel of pure expression overhead) and carry almost no signal; the 10 large cases (core_us 397 us - 117.8 ms) are scalar-pipe bound in the gather, NOT bandwidth bound (see above). geomean_subsets records both groups separately so the 50-case figure is not read as one homogeneous number. CONTAMINATION, judged by the four-field method (host-derived Task Duration vs core counters), not by magnitude and not by load average: kept op_summary for cases 0/24/40/44 (4 orders of magnitude apart) shows every kernel AI_VECTOR_CORE with aicore_time = 0 throughout; Task Wait Time is BINARY -- either ~0 (0.00-7.02 us) or a constant 10102-10278 us, i.e. the instrumented 10 ms sync+sleep separator, constant to 3-4 significant figures within each case and carried by exactly one Cast per iteration; and aiv_time/Task Duration is 0.96/0.98/0.96 for GatherElementsV2/Add/Pack on case 44, dropping to 0.69-0.79 only on the sub-3 us micro-kernels where the fixed launch cost dominates. Verdict REAL, not host inflation. One 12657 us Wait outlier appears in case 40 with every surrounding Duration nominal, which is a host hiccup rather than queue contention. MFU: see flops_note in each case. flops_analytic counts ONLY the per-channel index bias (3 adds per offset) because the gather, the int64 promotion and the Pack are addressing/movement, so MFU is structurally ~0 and max_mfu_pct = 0.001119463% is NOT comparable with the shipped 1.4142651e-08%, which came from a literal flops=1.0 placeholder. That said, do not read this as merely 'the wrong peak is registered': for this operator NO peak is a meaningful denominator. Measured iteration-level vector-ALU occupancy is 9.8% (case 0) and 7.3% (case 24) on the launch-floor cases, falling to 1.66% (case 40) and 1.70% (case 44) on the large ones -- i.e. on the cases that dominate the geomean the vector ALU is ~98% idle, so switching 19 from the cube peak to the vector peak would rescale a number that does not measure anything either way. The same is true on the bytes side, and this is the part that is easy to get wrong: bytes_moved is ALGORITHMIC in/out only. Folding the chain's intermediates in would NOT fix it, because that figure is only a loose upper bound -- case 44's ~2416 MB over 117.8 ms is 20.5 TB/s, above this part's ~1.2-1.4 TB/s, so those intermediates are not all HBM round-trips (images_flat is only 6.29 MB and is plausibly L2-resident). So achieved_bw_gbs here is a strict LOWER bound, the chain figure a loose upper bound, and NEITHER is comparable with sibling operators. Quote the per-kernel pipe breakdown instead. CASES 5/6/7/9/17/18/19/20/21 carry values from an extended w100/r40 window after failing the |drift|<=5% gate at the modal w25/r10. This is a genuine residual warm-up ramp, not a noise floor: all nine were still descending at w25/r10, the same-case paired A/B moves them by 6.3-8.8%, and all nine converge at w100/r40 with their last-30 10-block means flat to <0.5%. The 41 cases left at w25/r10 are consequently biased HIGH by at most 8.8% while the nine re-measured ones are not -- that asymmetry is why the paired bound is recorded in window_mix rather than left null.
